subject.title: Santee — Measure Y (Santee Local Services & Infrastructure Sales Tax Measure)

text: “To provide funding for City of Santee services and infrastructure, such as fixing streets and potholes; keeping streets, sidewalks, parks and public facilities safe, clean, and well-maintained; repairing / replacing aging infrastructure and stormdrains; local traffic management; fire protection, paramedic, crime prevention, and 911 emergency response, shall City of Santee’s measure establishing a one cent sales tax be adopted, providing approximately $14,000,000 annually for city services for 10 years, with independent audits, citizens’ committee oversight, and all funds locally controlled?”
This measure requires Simple Majority (50%+1) of those voting on the measure.
A “yes” vote on Measure “Y” will authorize the 1% transactions and use (sales) tax for 10 years.
A “no” vote on Measure “Y” will not authorize the 1% transactions and use (sales) tax for 10 years.

strong: 1% GENERAL TRANSACTIONS AND USE (SALES) TAX FOR

text: On June 24, 2026, the City Council voted to place Measure “Y” on the November 3, 2026 General Municipal Election ballot.

If approved by a majority of Santee voters, this Measure would authorize a one percent (1%) retail transactions and use (sales) tax within the City of Santee. It is estimated that Measure “Y” will provide an additional $14,000,000 in annual local funding for ten (10) years that could be used for City of Santee services and infrastructure, including repairing streets and potholes; cleaning and maintaining streets, sidewalks, parks and public facilities, repairing and replacing stormdrains, local traffic management, fire protection, paramedic, crime prevention, and 911 emergency response. This tax would be a “general tax,” meaning that revenues raised from the tax would go into the City’s general fund to pay for any lawful City program, improvement, or service.

The California Constitution (Proposition 218) and Revenue and Taxation Code section 7285.9 authorize the City to levy a general transactions and use/sales tax at a rate of one percent (1%) so long as the tax is approved by a majority of the voters voting in an election on that issue. If approved, the tax would become operative on April 1, 2027 and remain in effect for ten (10) years until it expires on March 31, 2037. Any extension of this tax beyond that date would require majority voter approval at a future City election.

Measure “Y” establishes a five (5) member Citizens’ Oversight Committee consisting of Santee residents, property owners and business owners appointed by the City Council. The Committee shall hold meetings open to the public pursuant to the California Brown Act. Each year, City staff shall present a proposed annual spending plan to the Committee, identifying City improvements, projects, programs, services proposed to be funded with Measure “Y” revenues. The Committee may make recommendations about the spending plan, which shall be incorporated into the City Manager’s proposed annual budget and subject to City Council approval.

The Committee shall also be authorized to independently review the City’s annual financial audit identifying Measure “Y” revenues collected and the expenditures made from such revenues in the prior year. The Committee shall report their findings publicly, including any concerns over use of Measure “Y” revenues, through an annual report presented to the City Council at a public meeting.

The tax would be paid in addition to current sales taxes and would be collected at the same time and in the same manner as existing sales taxes. All revenues raised by the tax would remain in the City and would not be shared with the State, County or any other agency.

text:
/s/ SHAWN HAGERTY
City Attorney

Some will say the City should live within its means. It does. Santee runs a lean, conservative budget, and the San Diego County Taxpayers Association agrees as noted in their endorsement of the measure.

Santee’s infrastructure needs have grown while the operating budget has not kept pace. We all drive the same streets. We all see the potholes and the wear on our roads. And we all expect that when we call 911, help arrives fast. These are services residents count on every day.

Measure Y is a one cent local sales tax. By state law it cannot be charged on groceries or prescription medications, so it does not fall on necessities. Visitors who shop here help pay too. A resident advisory committee and independent polling set the priorities for funding:
Citywide pavement repairs
New Fire Station at Woodglen Vista to address response times
Renovation of 55 year old Fire Station 4 (Cottonwood Ave)
Two new fire engines
Citywide storm drain replacements
Restoration of 8 city bridges
Citywide park improvements
The measure establishes an independent citizen oversight committee to safeguard spending and the tax would sunset after 10 years.
The cost of doing nothing is NOT zero. Every year that major projects are delayed, construction costs increase, infrastructure continues to deteriorate, and future solutions become more expensive.
Measure Y is how Santee gets ahead of this: repair what is failing now, before it becomes a costly emergency.
Vote YES on Measure Y.

text: Don’t be fooled, Santee friends and neighbors!

The City wants to minimize Measure Y by calling it a “1-cent” tax. While technically true, it means 1% of every taxable dollar you spend for the next 10 years! Overnight, gas will cost 5 cents more per gallon, a new car another $500, and everyday shopping and dining will increase. For Santee families, those added costs will total thousands over the life of this tax!

But the bigger question is: Can we trust the City to responsibly manage the money it already receives? An independent July 2026 audit of City travel expenses found significant policy violations, including the mayor, councilmembers, and staff receiving mileage payments while also receiving taxpayer-funded monthly car allowances.
If the City struggles to follow basic financial policies, how can we trust it with millions more of our hard-earned money?

The City also promotes an “independent” oversight committee as a safeguard. But its members are appointed by the very Council proposing this tax. The committee has no authority to stop or reject how the Council spends the money. It can only make recommendations, while the Council retains final say - including spending on things unrelated to the projects they claim this tax would fund. That’s hardly independent or accountable.
Santee families deserve competency and accountability at City Hall. Shifting the burden to the residents is not the answer!
Vote NO on Measure Y to keep Santee affordable and ensure city leaders remain accountable!

text: Measure Y has been vetted and endorsed by longtime residents and elected leaders, the Santee Mobilehome Owners Action Committee, the Santee Firefighters Association and the San Diego County Taxpayers Association.
Know the facts before voting:
FACT: Measure Y secures vital funding for streets, pothole repairs, sidewalks, storm drains, fire facilities, and parks. Some facilities are decades old and were built before Santee was even a city.
FACT: Measure Y ensures firefighters and paramedics can respond quickly to 911 emergencies.

FACT: Measure Y requires a local citizens’ oversight committee to publicly review and verify all spending, and independent audits. This is why the San Diego County Taxpayers Association endorsed Measure Y.

FACT: The City annually hires a certified public accounting firm to conduct independent audits, which have found no irregularities. The City has been recognized nationally for 21 consecutive years for excellence in financial management.
FACT: Measure Y by law, requires that every dollar raised by Measure Y be spent in Santee. No funds can be taken by the State or used elsewhere in San Diego County.
FACT: Essential purchases including groceries, prescription medicines, and diapers are exempt from Measure Y.
Measure Y is about safer streets, reliable infrastructure, and stronger emergency services.
Measure Y is temporary. The needs are not. The longer we take to address these vital infrastructure needs, the more they will cost.
Vote Yes on Y to protect the quality of life that makes Santee a great place to live.
